This Low-Level Design (LLD) document specifies the concrete system architecture, module interfaces, algorithmic workflows, and implementation details for the Knowledge Graph-enabled Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG) pipeline. The architecture is composed of three core technical components:
(1) an offline Graph Partitioning Module utilizing community detection algorithms (e.g., Leiden) to segment large-scale Knowledge Graphs into semantically coherent subgraphs;
(2) an online Hybrid Retrieval Mechanism combining dense vector embeddings with sparse term-matching (BM25) to evaluate and rank subgraph partitions against incoming user queries; and

(3) a Query-Aware Subgraph Traversal Algorithm that selectively expands nodes and extracts relevant triples to construct concise context prompts for the LLM. Each component is defined with explicit class structures, data flows, and interface signatures required for end-to-end execution.

The purpose of this Low-Level Design (LLD) document is to detail the technical architecture, component designs, algorithms, and integration workflow for the Knowledge Graph-enabled Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG) system. It serves as a guide for implementation, benchmarking, and module-level testing, establishing clear operational parameters for graph partitioning, hybrid semantic search, query-aware subgraph traversal, and context integration for LLMs.

The proposed system uses GraphRAG with weighted graph partitioning to improve knowledge retrieval. Wikidata5M entities are converted into vector embeddings, and edge weights are calculated using entity similarity. Weighted Leiden partitioning is applied, followed by resolution tuning and grouping small partitions to maintain a minimum size of 150 nodes. Each subgraph is indexed using embeddings and BM25 for hybrid retrieval. Given a user query, the system retrieves the top five relevant subgraphs and traverses them to extract relevant information. The approach depends on embedding quality, graph connectivity, and the effectiveness of the retrieval and partitioning strategies.
Algorithm: Weighted Graph Partitioning and Hybrid Subgraph Retrieval
Calculate similarity-based weights for graph edges.
Tune the resolution parameter and group small partitions to ensure a minimum size of 150 nodes.
Generate embeddings and BM25 indexes for each subgraph.
Convert the user query into an embedding and BM25 representation.
Retrieve and rank the top five subgraphs using hybrid similarity matching.
Traverse the selected subgraphs and extract relevant entities and relationships.
